title: Witness G with one lemma per property for Goedel's first incompleteness theorem
intent: Prove Goedel's first incompleteness theorem — every ω-consistent system T extending NN has a closed formula independent of T — by fixing the fixed-point sentence G once (line 66) and delegating each conjunct of `independent T G ∧ closed G` to its own named lemma, leaving a 10-line glue that poses the three lemmas and closes by `repeat split; tauto`.

parent.name: Goedel'sIncompleteness1st
parent.statement:
Theorem Goedel'sIncompleteness1st :
 wConsistent T ->
 exists f : Formula, independent T f /\ closed f.

children.name: freeVarG
children.closed_by: unfolds `closed` and `G`, destructs the fixed point, and for any `v` in the free variables proves both `v ≠ 0` (via `in_remove_neq`) and `v = 0` (via `freeVarCodeSysPrf` through `freeVarRepT`), closing `absurd (v = 0)`

children.name: FirstIncompletenessA
children.statement: Lemma FirstIncompletenessA : SysPrf T G -> Inconsistent LNN T.
children.closed_by: unfolds `G` to the fixed point `x` and proves `Inconsistent` with `contradiction with x`; `SysPrf T x` is the assumption, and `SysPrf T (notH x)` follows from the fixed-point equivalence (`cp2`, `iffE1`) and `codeSysPfCorrect` (`impE`, `nnI`)

children.name: FirstIncompletenessB
children.statement:
Lemma FirstIncompletenessB :
  wConsistent T -> ~ SysPrf T (notH G).
children.closed_by: assumes `SysPrf T (notH G)`, uses w-consistency (`wCon2Con`) to reach a numeral whose formula is not provable, then splits on `eq_nat_dec (checkPrf …) 0`: `= 0` contradicts via `codeSysPrfCorrect3` and `checkPrfCorrect1`; `≠ 0` reconstructs a proof of `x` via `checkPrfCorrect2` and yields inconsistency via `codeSysPrfCorrect2`

applicability.goal_shape: ∃ f : Formula, P f where P f is a conjunction (here `independent T f ∧ closed f`, i.e. `~ SysPrf T f ∧ ~ SysPrf T (~ f)%fol ∧ closed f`) and the witness f is a named term G defined once outside the proof; each conjunct of P G is discharged by one named lemma stated for G
applicability.use_when: the witness can be fixed up front (a fixed-point or constructed object) and the properties it must satisfy are independent of one another, each a self-contained statement; then the main proof is `exists G` plus `repeat split; tauto` over the posed lemmas
applicability.avoid_when: the witness must be adjusted during the proof, or the properties are interdependent (one lemma needs another's conclusion), or the property statements do not factor into separate named lemmas

claims.claim: The parent closes in 10 lines: after `exists G`, it poses `freeVarG`, `FirstIncompletenessA`, `FirstIncompletenessB`, asserts `~ Inconsistent LNN T` (discharged by `wCon2Con`), and `repeat split; tauto` resolves all three conjuncts of `independent T G ∧ closed G` from those three lemmas.
The main proof is 10 lines (292-301) while the three children span 19, 16 and 153 proof lines (88-106, 109-124, 134-286), so the glue hides 188 lines of argument behind three lemma names.

The author documents why FirstIncompletenessB is stated as `wConsistent T -> ~ SysPrf T (notH G)` rather than as a direct inconsistency implication: 'I don't believe I can prove (SysPrf T (notH G))->(wInconsistent T). So instead I prove:'

Each of the three children closes independently: freeVarG uses only the fixed point and `freeVarCodeSysPrf`, FirstIncompletenessA uses `codeSysPfCorrect`, FirstIncompletenessB uses `wCon2Con` and `codeSysPrfCorrect2/3`; no child cites another child.

consequences: The move creates one obligation per conjunct of the witness's spec — here `closed G`, `~ SysPrf T G` and `~ SysPrf T (notH G)` — surfaced by `repeat split`, plus the obligation that the witness G is well-typed/well-defined (here discharged once by the fixed-point construction `FixPointLNN`). All the real work is deferred to the children, so the theorem fails if any child is unprovable or is stated slightly weaker than the conjunct, in which case `tauto` cannot use it. The glue itself does no case analysis beyond the final `repeat split`.
